title: Write a GitHub Actions CI Workflow From Scratch
intro: The CI/CD tutorials had you driving existing workflows. Now write one: a pipeline that runs your tests on every push to main and on every pull request.

steps.prompt: Write a workflow named 'CI' that triggers on pushes to the 'main' branch and on any pull_request. It has one job called 'test' running on ubuntu-latest, with steps that: (1) check out the code with actions/checkout@v4, (2) set up Node 20 with actions/setup-node@v4, (3) run 'npm ci', (4) run 'npm test'.
apply_commands: git add ci.yml && git commit -m "add ci" && git push
steps.hint: Top-level keys: name, on, jobs. 'on' has push (with branches: [main]) and pull_request (can be empty). Under jobs.test: runs-on, then steps — a list where each item has either 'uses' (an action, optionally with a 'with:' block) or 'run' (a shell command). Checkout must be the first step: nothing else can see your code until it runs.
steps.solution:
name: CI
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test
steps.fake_output:
Workflow 'CI' registered. Run #1 queued on push to main.
  ✓ test  (1m 42s)
steps.explanation: Every push to main and every pull request now runs your tests automatically in a clean Ubuntu VM.
steps.why: 'npm ci' rather than 'npm install' is deliberate: ci installs exactly what package-lock.json says and fails if it's out of sync, which is what you want in CI — reproducible installs, not quietly updated ones (see cicd-tutorial-008). Checkout comes first because a fresh runner starts with an empty workspace.
